rows.title: FAA orders grounding of certain Boeing 737 Max 9 planes after Alaska Airlines incident
rows.standfirst: Alaska Airlines is inspecting all of its Boeing 737 Max 9 planes. United Airlines will also ground some of its jets. Meanwhile, Southwest and American said they do not carry the affected model.

rows.title: Higher wages, fewer temp workers and indicators of the year results
rows.standfirst: The U.S. economy added a solid number of jobs, the unemployment rate held steady, and a lot of people got raises. But, today we ask whether fewer temporary workers could mean recession, and whether higher wages might cause interest rates to stay high.

rows.title: The case of the serial sinking Spanish ships
rows.standfirst: Picture the Pacific Ocean of the 16th century. Spanish Galleons sail the wide open seas, carrying precious cargo like silver, porcelain, and textiles. The waters are dangerous; ship logs show concerns over pirates. But pirates are not to blame for a mysterious event that keeps happening.

rows.title: Azerbaijan names a former oil executive to lead 2024 climate talks
rows.standfirst: Mukhtar Babayev, has been named to lead the United Nations' annual climate talks later this year, prompting concern from some climate activists over his former ties to the state oil company.

rows.title: FDA approves Florida's plan to import cheaper drugs from Canada
rows.standfirst: The Food and Drug Administration's authorization of Florida's plan to import prescription medicines from Canada is a first. But the state still has hurdles to clear before imports could begin.

rows.title: U.S. unemployment has been under 4% for the longest streak since the Vietnam War
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 216,000 jobs in December, as the unemployment rate held steady at 3.7%. The labor market proved resilient in 2023, despite rising interest rates.

rows.title: Hershey sued for $5M over missing 'cute' face on Reese's Peanut Butter Pumpkins
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit claims the packaging shows "explicit carved out artistic designs" that the chocolate inside doesn't have.

rows.title: TGI Fridays closes dozens of its stores
rows.standfirst: The company is offering over 1,000 transfer opportunities for 80% of the impacted employees, it said. It additionally sold eight locations across the Northeast to its former CEO.

rows.title: WTF is a bitcoin ETF?
rows.standfirst: On today's show, we find out what the buzz is around something called a "spot bitcoin exchange-traded fund." Despite a volatile year for cryptocurrency companies, U.S. federal regulators are expected to approve this new financial product. So WTF is a bitcoin ETF?

rows.title: The U.S. Mint releases new commemorative coins honoring Harriet Tubman
rows.standfirst: The designs featured on the coins honor Tubman's life and her work as an abolitionist and social activist. The coins include $5 gold coins, $1 silver coins and half-dollar coins.

rows.title: Where the Republican presidential candidates stand on the economy
rows.standfirst: GOP presidential hopefuls know that the economy is an important issue — if not the top issue — for voters. That means it's a big talker on the campaign trail and a focus area for winning votes.

rows.title: After the Surfside collapse, Florida is seeing a new condo boom
rows.standfirst: The 2021 collapse killed nearly 100 people. Regulations passed since then have raised costs for those living in older buildings. Developers want homeowners to sell so they can put up luxury condos.

rows.title: What a pot of gumbo can teach us about disinflation
rows.standfirst: News about inflation made a lot of noise in the past two years, but the national CPI reports seem to indicate that inflation is starting to normalize within the Federal Reserve's target range. However, the national CPI basket of goods can have trouble representing inflation at a local level.

rows.title: Ford is recalling more than 112,000 F-150 trucks that could roll away while parked
rows.standfirst: The truck's rear axle hub bolt could break and cause the axle hub splines to become damaged, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration says.

rows.title: Red Sea tensions spell trouble for global supply chains
rows.standfirst: The Red Sea is a crucial piece of the global supply chain, accounting for around 15% of the world's shipping. This includes oil tankers and massive container ships transporting everything from microchips to furniture. Recent attacks by Houthi rebels, backed by Iran, have destabilized the region and prompted the U.S. to organize a multinational naval force to protect commercial ships. Today on the show, what's going on with shipping in the Red Sea.

rows.title: Tennis balls are causing arm injuries, top players say. Now, a review is underway
rows.standfirst: Professional tennis players are increasingly vocal in claims that the lack of consistency in balls used in tournaments is linked to elbow and wrist injuries.

rows.title: Current best practices for resume writing
rows.standfirst: LIfe Kit has tips on how to improve your resume.

rows.title: As the auto industry pivots to EVs, product tester Consumer Reports learns to adjust
rows.standfirst: The auto industry is adding more electric vehicles, and Consumer Reports' product reviewers are making adjustments too, from installing EV chargers to inventing new tests for cars.

rows.title: Sushi restaurants are thriving in Ukraine, bringing jobs and a 'slice of normal life'
rows.standfirst: Ukraine's economy is battered by Russia's full-scale invasion, but its consumer economy is still running — especially the country's popular sushi restaurants, where cream cheese is a key ingredient.

rows.title: The Maine Potato War of 1976
rows.standfirst: When you think of a potato, one state probably comes to mind: Idaho. But for much of American history, Maine was home to the nation's largest potato crop.

rows.title: The FAA is tightening oversight of Boeing and will audit production of the 737 Max 9
rows.standfirst: Regulators say they're increasing control of Boeing production after a panel blew off a 737 Max 9 jet, and will re-examine whether the company can be trusted to assess the safety of its own planes.

rows.title: A recent lawsuit alleges 'excessive' defects at Boeing parts supplier
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit doesn't specifically mention door plug systems like the one that failed last week. But it adds to the scrutiny of Spirit AeroSystems, which has been linked to other problems.

rows.title: The war in Gaza has taken an economic toll on tech, Israel's most productive sector
rows.standfirst: Reservists have been called into military service, leaving tech companies understaffed. The tech sector employs about 12% of Israel's workforce and accounts for half of the country's exports.

rows.title: This week's news quiz separates the winners from the losers. Which will you be?
rows.standfirst: Barbie lost the Golden Globe, a plane lost a door, Tiger Woods and Nike lost each other, and Chris Christie decided not to lose. There were also some winners this week.

rows.title: eBay will pay a $3 million fine over former employees' harassment campaign
rows.standfirst: The penalty settles charges against eBay more than three years after then-employees sent spiders and cockroaches, among other things, to a couple over their newsletter's coverage of the company.

rows.title: The lawsuit that could shake up the rental market
rows.standfirst: A number of lawsuits against Texas-based company RealPage are putting increased attention on how algorithms can interact with the rental market. In the lawsuit, RealPage is accused of facilitating a cartel between major property managers that results in higher prices for renters and increased profits for landlords who use RealPage's software. RealPage, however, denies any wrongdoing.

rows.title: As car insurance continues to rise, U.S. inflation ticks up in December
rows.standfirst: Overall CPI in December was up 3.4% from a year ago. The cost of motor vehicle insurance rose 1.5% in December from November, marking a 20.3% increase compared to the previous year.

rows.title: Alaska Airlines cancels all flights on the Boeing 737 Max 9 through Saturday
rows.standfirst: The airline said that it would cancel 110 to 150 flights a day while the Max 9 planes remain grounded, as signs indicate some travelers may at least temporarily try to avoid flying on Max 9 jetliners.

rows.title: Why oil in Guyana could be a curse
rows.standfirst: In 2015, Guyana changed forever when ExxonMobil discovered major oil deposits off its coast. The impoverished South American country known for its thick rainforest was suddenly on course to sudden wealth.

rows.title: The Universal Basic Income experiment in Kenya
rows.standfirst: There's this fundamental question in economics that has proven really hard to answer: What's a good way to help people out of poverty? The old-school way was to fund programs that would support very particular things, like buying cows for a village, giving people business training, or building schools.

rows.title: State-backed Russian hackers accessed senior Microsoft leaders' emails, company says
rows.standfirst: Microsoft says hackers broke into its corporate email system and accessed the accounts of members of its leadership team, as well as those of employees on its cybersecurity and legal teams.

rows.title: As Houthi attacks on ships escalate, experts look to COVID supply chain lessons
rows.standfirst: Shipping experts hope lessons learned during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Suez Canal disruption in 2021 and Somali pirate attacks more than a decade ago will mitigate widespread problems this time.

rows.title: Econ Battle Zone: Disinflation Confrontation
rows.standfirst: After very high inflation, the United States is finally feeling some relief in the form of "disinflation." But, why exactly has inflation slowed down?

rows.title: Walmart scams, expensive recycling, and overdraft fees
rows.standfirst: It is Friday. And Indicators of the Week is back — Plastics Edition. Today, we dig into how fraudsters have used Walmart gift cards to scam consumers out of more than $1 billion. We also find out why recycled plastic is actually more expensive now than newly produced plastic. And we learn how overdraft fees might be going way down.

rows.title: The S&P 500 surges to a record high as hopes about the economy — and Big Tech — grow
rows.standfirst: The index surged over 1% to hit a record high, surpassing the previous peak hit around two years ago, driven by big gains in large tech companies and by hopes about the economy.

rows.title: 'Sports Illustrated' to lay off most of its staff amid severed licensing deal
rows.standfirst: The union representing the magazine's staff said that SI's publisher plans to cut "a significant number, possibly all" of its union-represented staff.

rows.title: 2023 was the worst year to buy a house since the 1990s. But there's hope for 2024
rows.standfirst: Realtors hope it will be easier to buy a house in 2024. It can't get much harder: last year was one of the slowest on record thanks to high mortgage rates coupled with a housing shortage.

rows.title: Boeing 747 cargo plane with reported engine trouble makes emergency landing in Miami
rows.standfirst: A plane flown by Atlas Air experienced an engine malfunction and made an emergency landing at Miami International Airport shortly after takeoff. A witness said she saw sparks shooting from the plane.

rows.title: A rising tide of infrastructure funding floats new hope for Great Lakes shipping
rows.standfirst: Trains and trucks move the bulk of goods across the U.S. Some sailors say the Great Lakes waterways are underused shipping options and hope $17 billion of federal investment can help revitalize them.

rows.title: German government wants companies to 'de-risk' from China, but business is reluctant
rows.standfirst: Tough new rhetoric on China from some members of Germany's governing coalition has led to disagreement rather than unity on what the government's policy should be.

rows.title: From things that suck to stars that shine — it's the weekly news quiz
rows.standfirst: This week, we saw the Iowa caucuses suck up news coverage, an ancient space entity suck in stars, and low temps suck the charge from Teslas. Were you paying attention?

rows.title: In this Oklahoma town, almost everyone knows someone who's been sued by the hospital
rows.standfirst: U.S. hospitals face growing scrutiny over aggressive debt collection tactics. At one community hospital, few patients get financial aid when they can't afford to pay. Many more are taken to court.

rows.title: 'Cozy' relationship between Boeing and the U.S. draws scrutiny amid 737 Max 9 mess
rows.standfirst: The latest safety lapse at Boeing renews concerns about the company's influence in Washington and whether federal regulators have delegated too much of their oversight authority to its employees.

rows.title: Five tips for understanding political polls this election season
rows.standfirst: Election season is upon us, and so is the barrage of election polls. What differentiates a good poll from a bad one? How can we be smarter poll consumers? Today on the show, a couple of polling experts give us their top tips.

rows.title: The Cozy Relationship Between Boeing and the Federal Government
rows.standfirst: These days when you think of Boeing, the words that come to mind might be: door plug, 737-max, grounded. But before this month's safety debacle and the Ethiopian and Lion Air crashes five years ago, Boeing was synonymous with industry and innovation, and the company enjoyed a special relationship with the U.S. government and U.S. presidents.

rows.title: House passes bipartisan tax bill to expand child tax credit
rows.standfirst: The bill includes $33 billion to expand the widely used child tax credit for three years — including the tax season currently underway, provided the bill quickly passes the Senate.

rows.title: The Chicken Tax (Classic)
rows.standfirst: Note: This episode originally ran in 2015 .

rows.title: A federal judge dismisses Disney's lawsuit against Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis
rows.standfirst: The judge says Disney lacked standing to sue Florida's governor on First Amendment grounds after DeSantis removed Disney's self-governing status after the company's CEO spoke out about a Florida law.

rows.title: How to transform a war economy for peacetime
rows.standfirst: In the 1980s, California was the heart of the aerospace industry. But when the Cold War ended, military spending cuts put those defense jobs in jeopardy.

rows.title: Boeing declines to give a financial outlook as it focuses on quality and safety
rows.standfirst: In a call with investors, Boeing's CEO didn't offer a financial outlook for 2024. He said the company is focused on quality and safety after a fuselage panel blew off a 737 Max-9 jet in midair.

rows.title: The Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady but signals rate cuts may be coming
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, but indicated that rates could fall in the coming months if inflation continues to cool.

rows.title: Taylor Swift, Drake, BTS and more may have their music taken off TikTok — here's why
rows.standfirst: Universal Music Group, the world's largest music company, has threatened to remove all of the music it owns from TikTok, unless the streaming platform agrees to more favorable terms.

rows.title: PGA Tour strikes a $3 billion deal with a sports owners investment group
rows.standfirst: The PGA Tour is getting a $3 billion investment from Strategic Sports Group in a deal that would give players access to more than $1.5 billion as equity owners in the new PGA Tour Enterprises.

rows.title: 'You have blood on your hands,' senator tells Mark Zuckerberg for failing kids online
rows.standfirst: The top tech executives from Meta, X, TikTok, Snap and Discord get the fifth degree from the Senate Judiciary Committee.

rows.title: Elon Musk cannot keep Tesla pay package worth more than $55 billion, judge rules
rows.standfirst: Elon Musk is not entitled to landmark compensation package awarded by Tesla's board of directors that is potentially worth more than $55 billion, a Delaware judge ruled Tuesday.

rows.title: Can Just-In-Time handle a new era of war?
rows.standfirst: Just-in-time manufacturing began as a way to save space, remove costs and improve efficiency ... for Toyota. The U.S. defense industry has since incorporated this approach. Now, leaders in the defense industry question whether it's to blame for weapons and ammunition shortages.

rows.title: Toyota says 50,000 U.S. vehicles are unsafe to drive due to defective air bags
rows.standfirst: Toyota issued a "Do Not Drive" advisory for thousands of older models in the U.S., warning that a faulty air bag inflator has the potential to explode and seriously injure drivers or passengers.

rows.title: What to know about Elon Musk's Neuralink, which put an implant into a human brain
rows.standfirst: "Imagine if Stephen Hawking could communicate faster than a speed typist or auctioneer," Musk said as he announced the step. "That is the goal."

rows.title: The IRS got $80B to help people and chase rich tax avoiders. Here's how it's going
rows.standfirst: Commissioner Danny Werfel says the IRS is seeing "very powerful early results" in its efforts to improve enforcement on high wealth is paying off.

rows.title: UPS is cutting 12,000 jobs just months after reaching union deal
rows.standfirst: UPS will cut 12,000 jobs and released a revenue outlook for this year that sent its shares down sharply. CEO Carol Tome said that the job cuts will produce $1 billion in cost savings.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
